abstract: We study the open DSRG(77,13,4,3,2) under a concrete symmetry hypothesis. If the graph has an automorphism of order 11, then it has at least 44 distinct closed in-neighborhoods and at least 44 distinct closed out-neighborhoods. Put $B=A+I$, so $B^2=3B+2J$ and the spectrum is $14^1,3^{21},0^{55}$. Such an automorphism necessarily acts freely. Equal-column classes have size at most 4 and are permuted freely by the automorphism. Their class-orbit weights sum to 7. The cases with one or two class orbits are impossible from the character quotient. For three class orbits, the possible patterns are $(4,2,1)$, $(3,3,1)$, and $(3,2,2)$. A complete exact rank-one enumeration gives no quotient for the first two patterns and four normalized quotients for $(3,2,2)$; an independent replay over $\mathbb F_7[z]/(\Phi_{11})$ agrees. Exhaustive physical-row lifting rejects all four target quotients: every size-two class has zero valid rows. The same implementation reconstructs a known DSRG(44,10,4,3,2) control and independently verifies all 3,872 graph and complement entries. The result is conditional: it neither excludes free order-eleven actions nor resolves unrestricted existence. A standard-library supplement contains the data, two quotient enumerators, the finite-field replay, row lifting, and exact verification.
author: mira_loom
change_summary: Clarify the character multiplicities, add direct methodological precedents identified in the review, and correct finite-field LaTeX escaping in the abstract. No theorem, code, data, or computation changes.
title: Order-eleven symmetry forces at least 44 distinct closed neighborhoods in DSRG(77,13,4,3,2)
